subject: Anchor zone declaration and keystore handoff request
messages:
From: Claire Danvers <claire@medilabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medilabs.com
Date: 2027-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Anchor zone declaration & keystore handoff for Medilabs pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the performance numbers. Before we sign the pilot MPA we need a short evidence package for our security review focused on residency and private deployment controls. Specifically we need:

- A short statement confirming that for the pilot all customer data and inference workloads will be anchored in EU-West (no cross-region replicas or automatic failover).
- A redacted SOC 2 summary (scope and attestation date).
- Completed SIG/CAIQ matrix or equivalent mapping.
- Keystore/operator separation details and the runbook for keystore handoff/rotation.
- VPC peering endpoints (IP ranges) and the expected peering workflow.
- Operator inventory for the EU region (roles, base country, and whether any third-party operators have access).

We attached our short intake form to this email (Medilabs_Security_Intake_Form.pdf) that lists the items and who owns signoff. Could you confirm what you can share by EOD PT Wednesday and whether any items will require an NDA or redaction?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement would like the package to attach to the pilot MPA.

Best,
Claire
Claire Danvers
Head of Security, Medilabs
claire@medilabs.com

---
Attachments: Medilabs_Security_Intake_Form.pdf (application/pdf, 187KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Danvers <claire@medilabs.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Anchor zone declaration & keystore handoff for Medilabs pilot

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list and for sending the intake form. We'll assemble a concise package you can attach to the MPA. Quick responses up front:

- We can commit to anchoring the pilot to the EU-West zone (no automatic cross-region replicas or failover unless explicitly enabled and agreed in writing).
- We can provide a redacted SOC 2 summary and a completed SIG/CAIQ mapping.
- Keystore handoff and keystore-operator separation runbook is available; we will provide a handoff runbook + audit log excerpts.
- VPC peering endpoint details and a short peering playbook are available.
- Operator inventory for EU region will be provided; we will mark third-party vendors where applicable.

Irene (security/compliance) and Marissa (account lead for Medilabs) are looped in to drop the artifacts and confirm the operator roster.

Two clarifying Qs before we package everything:
1) Do you require an HSM attestation or is a keystore operator roster + audit logs sufficient for procurement?
2) For the residency statement, do you need explicit language about not enabling cross-region live failover, or is the anchor-zone commitment above sufficient?

If you can reply quickly on those two points we'll aim to deliver the initial package within 24 hours and finalize the formal region commitment letter by EOD Wednesday PT.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0198

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Danvers <claire@medilabs.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-15T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Anchor zone declaration & keystore handoff for Medilabs pilot

Claire — good morning. Answers to Mateo's Qs and attached artifacts below.

Short answers:
- HSM attestation: for this pilot, Medilabs indicated software keystore is acceptable; we will flag any HSM-related items as optional add-ons. If you require an HSM attestation we can escalate to Legal & Security and provide an additional certificate but that will add time.
- Residency language: we will provide an explicit signed region commitment letter that states "Redwood Inference will not enable cross-region live failover for customer workloads without prior written consent from the customer".

Attachments included in this message (redacted where required):
1) redwood_SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf (pdf, 156KB) — contains scope, auditor, and attestation date; we've redacted operationally sensitive IPs and internal service names.
2) SIG_matrix_MEDILABS.xlsx (spreadsheet, 310KB) — completed SIG mapping with control references and evidence pointers.
3) keystore-handshake-runbook.md (text, 24KB) — runbook describing keystore handoff, rotation cadence, and required tickets/approvals; includes the audit log fields we can export on request.
4) vpc-peering-endpoints.json (application/json, 6KB) — sample peering ranges and expected BGP/ACL notes (production ranges will be tenant-specific).
5) operator_inventory_eu.csv (text, 12KB) — list of operators, roles, home countries, and third-party flag. (Embedded in the SIG spreadsheet as well.)

A few notes of context so procurement understands limitations: we cannot publish internal operator location street addresses for security reasons; we provide base country and role and evidence of background checks where applicable. Third-party vendors are labeled and we include contract references.

On timeline: initial artifacts are attached. We will produce the signed region commitment letter and a short region-commitment appendix by EOD Wednesday PT. If you want the HSM attestation, please flag it today and we'll estimate the lead time.

--
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

---
Attachments: redwood_SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf; SIG_matrix_MEDILABS.xlsx; keystore-handshake-runbook.md; vpc-peering-endpoints.json; operator_inventory_eu.csv

From: Claire Danvers <claire@medilabs.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medilabs.com
Date: 2027-03-15T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Anchor zone declaration & keystore handoff for Medilabs pilot

Thanks Irene — this looks good. A couple quick follow-ups:

- Can you confirm in writing that the pilot's data and inference runtime will be pinned to eu-west-1 and that Redwood will not enable cross-region failover or replicas without written consent? (We need that sentence verbatim for procurement.)
- Please confirm there are no APAC-based operators with access to the keystore or the production tenant for this pilot. If any exist, please call them out explicitly.
- Procurement would like a DocuSign link to the MPA; if you can attach that link in the package it will speed approvals.

If you can send the two confirmations and the DocuSign link we can route for signature today.

Best,
Claire

Claire — thanks for the prompt review and the clear asks. Per Irene's attachments, please find the two explicit confirmations below that you can paste into procurement:

1) Region anchoring statement (signed by Redwood legal):
"Redwood Inference will anchor Medilabs' pilot workloads and associated persistent data in the EU-West (eu-west-1) cloud zone. Redwood will not enable automatic cross-region live failover, replica replication, or routing of production tenant data to regions outside EU-West unless explicitly authorized in writing by Medilabs via the Master Purchase Agreement or a signed amendment."

2) Operator access confirmation:
"Redwood confirms that for the Medilabs pilot the named operator roster provided (operator_roster_list.csv) contains only personnel with primary residence in EU or US timezones and that no APAC-based third-party operators have access to the keystore or production tenant. Any third-party vendor with access would be listed with contract references; none are listed for this pilot."

DocuSign link for the MPA: https://www.docusign.com/sign/MEDILABS-MPA-2027 (this is the signing endpoint for the pilot MPA; legal already pre-populated the appendix with the region commitment).

Attachments included with this mail: region_commitment_letter.pdf; operator_roster_list.csv

We'll also provide a short appendix that lists the audit fields we will share post-handoff and the expected SLO for keystore rotation events (30 days notice for rotation scripts during pilot).

If that language works I can have Legal countersign the commitment letter and send via DocuSign by EOD.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
